text:
natalie_cs: heads up — novahealth just pinged asking for a credit on INV-NEO-0903. they got a ~48% overage charge on their dedicated commit after an apac failover on 2026-03-09. customer says traffic was routed to failover region and burst costs spiked. can we review? :eyes:
liam_billing: pulling the invoice now. quick snapshot from our metering: `region: apac-sg`, `reserved_commit: 200k token-hrs`, `burst_used: 94k token-hrs`, `spike_window: 03/09 02:10 - 03/09 14:00 UTC` — looks like ~12h sustained increase. also see two failover events in routing logs.
audit-bot: automated note: failover reason = nodepool eviction in apac-us-central replication. incident ref: INC-APAC-6781.
natalie_cs: novahealth says their product team couldn't pre-warm capacity because the failover happened fast; they expect some SLA protection. they asked for full burst credit + waiver of late fee.
marie_finance: can we get a precise dollars number? what's the invoice line for the burst charge and how does it map to their reserved commit credit?
liam_billing: invoice line: `Burst overage: $18,275 (94,000 token-hrs x $0.194/hr equivalent)`; reserved commit discount applied elsewhere. if we fully credit burst they'd owe $0 for overage but invoice still shows baseline reserved fee.
sam_ae: NovaHealth is a mid-sized customer on an annual reserved contract. happy path is a one-time credit to preserve relationship, but we should avoid setting a blanket precedent. recommend offering a partial credit tied to SLA clause and require we finish the routing postmortem before approving full credit. :+1:
marie_finance: what's our SLA credit policy for dedicated failover? i recall we have a max of 30% monthly credit for sustained outages but nothing explicit for burst from failover.
liam_billing: correct — SLA doc lists latency/availability credits, not explicit dedicated-burst failure credits. we can treat this as a service degradation and apply a discretionary goodwill credit.
marie_finance: propose 35% credit on the burst line ($6,396) as a one-time goodwill, conditional on CS delivering the postmortem and customer acknowledging it's a one-time exception. i'll need a short approval note for audit.
natalie_cs: can do. i'll draft the customer message and attach the postmortem once the infra team finalizes it. do we need legal signoff?
sam_ae: legal not required for this amount, but ping solutions-eng to confirm there's no config/state we'll need to change for other customers. also cc sales ops so we capture precedent.
liam_billing: once we have the PM and acceptance, i'll create a credit memo and apply it to INV-NEO-0903. expected ledger entries: `CreditMemo: -$6,396` applied to `Invoice: INV-NEO-0903`.
audit-bot: reminder: tag credit memos with reason code `GOODWILL_FAILOVER_CREDIT` and attach postmortem before month close.
marie_finance: approved in principle. liam, please hold the credit until the postmortem is uploaded and cs confirms customer acceptance. finance will sign the approval note: "Finance approves one-time goodwill credit of $6,396 for NovaHealth (INV-NEO-0903) pending postmortem and customer confirmation)."
natalie_cs: noted. i'll send to novahealth now: offer 35% credit on burst line, include timeline for postmortem (ETA 48h), and require their acknowledgement that this is a one-time accommodation. will update thread when they reply. :email:
liam_billing: thanks — i'll prep the credit memo but not post. tagging @audit-bot for the ledger flag.
sam_ae: thanks team. small ask: can we include a short internal blurb about the customer outcome for the next sales call? helps AE to avoid surprises.
marie_finance: yes — once closed, share a one-paragraph summary and copy to sales-ops.
natalie_cs: will do. closing loop after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
